meta.title: NASA hazards, health effects and open gaps
meta.note: devHint_* fields are suggestions by the developer, not from the research.

hazards.effectOnBody: Raises cancer risk and can damage the central nervous system (cognition, motor function, behavior)
hazards.countermeasure: Protective shielding, dosimetry, alerts; research into medical countermeasures
hazards.sourceName: NASA HRP Hazards (also Space.com, GPSDaily summaries)

hazards.effectOnBody: Behavioral issues are expected when groups are confined for long periods
hazards.countermeasure: Lighting, movement and sleep help protect mental health

hazards.effectOnBody: About 20-minute communication delay each way to Mars; evacuation not an option
hazards.countermeasure: Crew medical autonomy and ground medical support

hazards.effectOnBody: Affects hand-eye coordination, balance, movement and sense of space
hazards.countermeasure: ISS astronauts exercise at least 2 hours/day (treadmill, ergometer, resistance equipment)

hazards.effectOnBody: Spacecraft is a machine as well as a home; its ecosystem shapes daily life
hazards.countermeasure: Extensive recycling of oxygen, water, carbon dioxide and waste

healthEffects.effect: Without gravity, bones break down and become more brittle, raising the chance of breaks
Weightlessness alters circulation and heart function, possibly raising cardiovascular event risk
healthEffects.countermeasure: Exercise; one study estimates up to 17% of astronauts could still have performance-limiting deconditioning

healthEffects.effect: Spaceflight stress can reactivate dormant viruses, causing rashes and other symptoms
Isolation, radiation, distance and other stressors can harm crew mental health
Nutrient stability over long missions is a concern
healthEffects.countermeasure: Better food formulation, processing, packaging and preservation

healthEffects.effect: Eye changes such as disc edema, choroidal folds and globe flattening

gaps.note: No numeric thresholds found in sources so far; sources only describe the flight surgeon's role. Mark as 'to be confirmed from NASA resources' - do not invent cut-offs.
gaps.referenceRoleOnly: CSA: role of a flight surgeon

gaps.note: No single page compares these; search the Human Research Roadmap by risk (e.g. Hostile/Closed Environment hazard).
